object_description: compact block filling the perimeter depth, graded back from the third floor upwards
geometry_property: graded volume from the third floor up
design_condition: the volume fits between the existing staff house and laboratory building, using the full depth of the perimeter to keep an appropriate distance from the neighbours and grading upwards to respond to their heights and the terrain jump

positive: The new building fits confidently between the existing staff house and laboratory building
Using the entire depth of the perimeter maintains an appropriate distance from the neighbouring buildings
Grading the volume from the third floor upwards subtly responds to the surrounding heights and the terrain jump
The staggering of the building is also an expression of the interior
The facade recesses have their functional consequence in the interior
The skilful organisation of the floor plans results in an interesting sectional solution
The three-storey central foyer gives the school its identity and becomes the heart of the complex
The two administrative floors above benefit from the open courtyard
A terrace for the cafeteria is planned on the sheltered intermediate area
The teaching floors are characterised by the central foyer and the life around this light space promises a good learning atmosphere
The two administrative floors are simple and functional
The construction and facade design proposals promise a concise and appropriate appearance in the neighbourhood
Generous well-proportioned windows, the ventilated facade and the materials point to a sustainable construction method
A compact volume with a balanced floor area ratio
The restrained facade with a cost-advantageous ratio of transparent surfaces has a corresponding effect
The project has the lowest construction costs and meets the brief very well
A very carefully detailed design that impresses with its pleasantly subtle simplicity
It integrates naturally into the existing quarter and could make a new mark on the street
negative: The entrance sequence is not ideal in terms of its accessibility and dimensions
The access doors to the toilet vestibules hardly correspond to the status intended by the foyer space
The distribution of course room types across the floors is not optimally mixed
The concept of learning islands only partially corresponds to that of the users
